note: Keystroke spike (SKR-109). Surrogate engine: Chromium. Constant-time tolerance: block-10k p99 <= 2x block-1.

stage3aConstantTime.note: Stage 3a absolute ceiling (SKR-215) for harness/block.matrix.spec.ts's 'the bespoke engine types constant-time' gate. bigP99CeilingMs caps the block-10k p99 in absolute terms -- the number that actually matters for feel, and (unlike the noisy block-1 baseline the ratio divides by) it was diagnosed as stable run to run. It pairs with, but does not replace, the ratio check in that spec. Regenerate by running `bun run test:latency -- -g "Stage 3a: the bespoke engine"` several times on a quiet machine, reading the '[3a] ... block-10k p99=' console line each run, and setting bigP99CeilingMs to roughly 1.6-1.8x the highest observed value -- tight enough to still catch a genuine regression (e.g. a doubling), loose enough to absorb machine-to-machine and CI jitter. Re-based 2026-07-09 (SKR-190): the id->index map removed the O(document) model work from the keystroke path; observed block-10k p99 now ~19-22ms (was ~20-28ms), the remaining cost being engine-side selection/layout.

stage3aDragSelect.note: SKR-190 drag-selection gate for harness/block.matrix.spec.ts's 'drag-selection stays within frame budget' spec. frameP95CeilingMs caps the p95 gap between consecutive animation frames while a real mouse drag extends a selection at 10k blocks. Before the SKR-190 id->index map and the range-scoped selectedLeaves, this measured ~2400ms per frame (O(n^2) per selectionchange frame); after, ~9ms. Regenerate like stage3aConstantTime: run `bun run test:latency -- -g "drag-selection"` several times on a quiet machine and set the ceiling to roughly 3x the highest observed p95.
